record.program_name: Project-Based Vouchers, Housing Authority of the City of Santa Ana (SAHA)
record.administering_agency: Housing Authority of the City of Santa Ana (Community Development Agency), waiting list hotline (714) 667-2284
record.typical_award_size: PBVs are committed to City-financed projects through the Affordable Housing Development RFP: Estrella Springs 89 PBVs (89 PSH units, former Budget Inn), WISEPlace on Broadway 25 PBVs (15 set aside for domestic violence survivors), Crossroads at Washington 15 PBVs (43 PSH units of 86), Richard Lehn Intergenerational Housing 8 PBVs (11 units, under construction), plus earlier commitments at Casa Querencia (57 units), Heroes' Landing (75), The Orchard (72) and FX Residences (17). PBV waiting lists for Crossroads at Washington and Andalucia closed April 30, 2026. SAHA received 25 Foster Youth to Independence vouchers in August 2025. Total HCV count not confirmed from an opened document.
record.affordability_requirement: PBV households at or below 50% AMI at admission (30% of adjusted income toward rent); PSH units generally 30% AMI with Coordinated Entry referrals; HAP contracts up to 20 years.
record.next_deadline: Request PBVs in the RFP quarterly rounds (next January 11, 2027); SAHA's FY 2026 Annual Plan draft (Feb 17, 2026) was opened but lists no fixed PBV allotment.
record.layering_notes: Santa Ana is one of four PHAs in Orange County (with OCHA, Anaheim and Garden Grove) and has been the most active in project-basing: 89 PBVs at Estrella Springs is the largest single PBV award in the county. A HAP contract is not itself a prevailing wage trigger but Davis-Bacon applies to new construction or rehab of nine or more PBV units and PBVs bring a HUD subsidy layering review. Combine with City HOME or Housing Successor loans, County MHSA/BHSA capital and OCHFT. The City also receives its own HHAP allocation (Richard Lehn used $2,021,319 HHAP), so the operating stack for PSH can be entirely city-controlled. PSH properties page, Housing Authority page, PBV waiting list notices and the 2025 Affordable Housing Awards release opened on santa-ana.gov.
record.cycle_notes: requested with or without capital in the Affordable Housing Development RFP
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal Davis-Bacon: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (PBV development requirements, labor standards) requires the owner and its contractors to pay Davis-Bacon wages in the case of development involving nine or more contract units, whether or not completed in stages (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153). Applies only to PBVs committed under a development agreement for new construction or rehab; PBVs placed on existing housing with 8 or fewer contract units, or no development activity, do not trigger it. State prevailing wage depends separately on other public funds in the deal under Labor Code 1720.
record.audit_note: Prevailing wage set true per 24 CFR 983.153(c): Davis-Bacon at 9+ PBV contract units in development; existing-housing PBVs are not covered.

record.administering_agency: City of Santa Ana Planning and Building Agency; designation issued by HCD
record.typical_award_size: Not a direct subsidy. Santa Ana appears on HCD's list of Prohousing Designated Jurisdictions, which gives projects inside the city bonus points or priority processing in AHSC, Infill Infrastructure Grant, Transformative Climate Communities, SCCP, LPP, TIRCP and STPG, and makes the City eligible for the Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP).
record.affordability_requirement: Follows the state program applied for (AHSC and IIG serve lower income projects at or below 80% AMI).
record.next_deadline: Designation is good for four years from award and must be renewed; PIP rounds are announced by HCD. Confirm the designation date with the Planning Division.
record.layering_notes: The only Prohousing city among the five Orange County priority cities (Anaheim, Irvine, Huntington Beach and Garden Grove are not on the list opened 2026-11-08), so AHSC and IIG applications in Santa Ana carry the designation points. The City's own HHAP allocation, SAHA PBVs and the RFP loans make a full local stack for AHSC-sized projects. HCD designated jurisdictions page opened.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) covers construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(b)(1)-(6) lists the forms public funds take (payments, construction by the agency, below-market asset transfers, reduced or waived fees and loans, contingent loans, credits). A Prohousing Designation (scoring points and eligibility for HCD programs) grants regulatory relief and provides none of those forms of public funds, and the law it rests on imposes no prevailing wage condition, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any City or state funds layered on the same project are tested separately. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

record.program_name: HOME, PLHA and CDBG entitlement funds used as affordable housing gap financing (Build More Homes Initiative)
record.administering_agency: City of Anaheim Housing and Community Development Department (HUD Programs division) and Anaheim Housing Authority
record.typical_award_size: HOME allocation FY 2024 $1,314,087.60 (down from $2,240,380 in FY 2010); PLHA about $3,000,000 a year since 2019; together about $4,600,000 a year of recurring production money, though a large share of HOME is committed to tenant-based rental assistance. City cash gap financing has averaged $6,000,000 per project on the last two developments (Finamore Place, 101 family units, completed February 2022; Miraflores, 85 PSH family units, 2024, with a 60-year ground lease, a $3,000,000 HOME loan and 8 vouchers). Center of Hope (72 PSH units, 2023) received a $2,000,000 City construction loan and 50 vouchers. Anaheim also administers CDBG, ESG and HOPWA for the region.
record.per_unit_cap: HOME: HUD maximum per-unit subsidy limits.
record.affordability_requirement: HOME rents and 80% AMI limits with 20% of HOME units at 50% AMI; PLHA rental production at or below 60% AMI; City deals have typically been 100% affordable family, senior or supportive housing with 55-year covenants.
record.next_deadline: Annual Action Plan adopted each spring; developer solicitations are issued per site (recent Housing Authority RFPs covered 212 S. Beach Blvd and State College at Lincoln). Verify the FY 2026-27 HOME and PLHA figures with the department; the City documents page lists only the FY 2022-23 Action Plan.
record.layering_notes: Anaheim does not run a competitive NOFA; it assembles sites (Beach Boulevard corridor, former motels) and selects developers by RFP, then layers HOME, PLHA, A-LHTF and Housing Authority PBVs. The City is an HHAP direct recipient and a HOPWA grantee for Orange County, so operating subsidies for PSH can come from the same department. Stack order seen in practice: City land lease plus HOME or PLHA loan, Housing Authority PBVs, County MHSA/BHSA or OCHFT loan, 4% credits with CMFA or CSCDA bonds. Davis-Bacon on HOME projects of 12 or more assisted units; state prevailing wage on all City funds. Figures from the June 2026 A-LHTF Guidelines PDF (opened); Housing and Community Development documents page and 2026 affordable housing fact sheet opened; Action Plan PDFs and CivicAlerts pages returned 403.
record.cycle_notes: project-specific RFPs and negotiated agreements; no standing developer NOFA
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

record.program_name: Affordable Housing In-Lieu Fee Fund (Irvine Zoning Ordinance Sec. 2-3-5.B.3.c; fee set by City Council resolution)
record.administering_agency: City of Irvine Community Development Department
record.typical_award_size: In-lieu fees are deposited in the City's affordable housing fund and used for projects implementing the Housing Element needs assessment or serving low, very low and extremely low income households; the fee is charged per market-rate unit under a Council-approved formula, determined at building permit, and has not been updated since 2011 (a legacy $17,000 per unit rate applied only to pre-2007 Irvine Business Complex filings). A May 2026 Draft Affordable Housing and In-Lieu Fee Analysis was released August 10, 2026; staff recommends keeping the existing formula with updated inputs. Finance Commission reviewed it October 19, 2026; Planning Commission and Council hearings are not yet scheduled. Fund balance and any developer allocation process are not published.
record.affordability_requirement: Fund uses limited to low, very low and extremely low income households and Housing Element implementation; recipients record 55-year covenants under Chapter 2-3.
record.next_deadline: No NOFA located as of November 8, 2026. In-lieu fee update pending Planning Commission and City Council hearings (dates TBD). Ask Community Development (cd@cityofirvine.org) for the fund balance and whether a developer round is planned.
record.layering_notes: Because most Irvine builders provide units on-site or through credits, the in-lieu fund is smaller than Santa Ana's; its visible use is land and loans to Irvine Community Land Trust projects (Salerno, Parc Derian, Doria, Alegre, Sage Park) which then take LIHTC, HOME, OCHFT and County MHSA money. Local and state funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so state prevailing wage applies unless a 1720(c) exemption fits the deal, such as 1720(c)(5)(E) for below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI (see prevailing_wage_basis). Code text read on zoneomics because the City-linked Municode page is Cloudflare-blocked; the City In-Lieu Fee Formula Update page (cityofirvine.gov/node/94569) and its September 8, 2026 FAQ were opened and confirm the 15% requirement, the formula-based fee and the update schedule.
eligible_project_detail: land for Irvine Community Land Trust projects
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Local loans can be public funds under 1720(b)(1), (b)(4) or (b)(5), but 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts privately owned residential projects whose only public participation is below-market loans with at least 40% of units restricted for 20 or more years at 80% AMI or below, and 1720(c)(3) exempts de minimis subsidy (under $600,000 and under 2% of total project cost). Irvine Zoning Ordinance Sec. 2-3-5 states no prevailing wage rule for in-lieu fee loans. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
record.audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: no program rule found stating prevailing wage applies; changed true to unclear because only the general 1720(b) public-funds definition supports it.

record.program_name: Affordable Housing Credits Program (Irvine Zoning Ordinance Sec. 2-3-6)
record.administering_agency: City of Irvine Community Development Department (credits database and three-party credits agreements)
record.typical_award_size: Market mechanism, not a subsidy. Projects that build more affordable units than the 15% requirement earn transferable credits in three income categories (extremely low or very low, low, moderate) that they may sell to market-rate projects or mixed projects with a shortfall; credits become available after building permits are issued for the excess units and a completion bond or certificate of occupancy is in place. A three-party credits agreement (buyer, seller, City) must be executed before the buyer's building permits; sale prices are not disclosed to the City.
record.affordability_requirement: Credits track the income level of the excess units; the receiving project satisfies its required affordable component at that level.
record.next_deadline: Agreement before building permit; City maintains the credits database on request.
record.layering_notes: Reclassified from other to regulatory requirement: the credits program is part of the Chapter 2-3 inclusionary procedure (15% requirement, 5% each extremely low or very low, low and moderate) and is a compliance-trading mechanism, not a public subsidy. For a 100% affordable developer it can still be a revenue source: excess units earn credits (for example 2.0 credits per ownership unit sold to lower income buyers, 1.6 extremely low or very low credits per qualifying rental unit, one credit releasing 19 market-rate units) that can be sold to market-rate builders. Confirm with the City how many credits are outstanding and the recent trading range. Read on the zoneomics mirror because the City-linked Municode page is Cloudflare-blocked; the City in-lieu fee page (cityofirvine.gov/node/94569) confirms the 15% requirement and menu options.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

record.program_name: Affordable Housing (Inclusionary Housing) Ordinance, Huntington Beach Zoning and Subdivision Ordinance Sec. 230.26, and in-lieu fee
record.administering_agency: City of Huntington Beach Community Development Department, Housing Division (Charles Kovac, Housing Manager, charles.kovac@surfcity-hb.org; Gregory Hoang, Senior Housing Analyst, 714-536-5473)
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. New residential projects of three or more units (including conversions) must restrict at least 10% of units: rental units at the lower income level (or very low or extremely low at the developer's choice), ownership units at moderate income, with fractional units rounded up or paid as fee. In-lieu fees may be paid by ownership projects of any size and rental projects of 100 units or fewer, per a fee schedule set by Council resolution and indexed annually to Orange County new home prices; fees are paid before building permit (pro rata for phased projects) and deposited in the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. Land dedication is allowed at Council discretion. Projects that exceed the requirement on-site are eligible for reduced City fees (the 2025 Annual Progress Report cites over $1,000,000 of development impact fee exemptions for a 78-unit project with 8 ELI, 32 VL and 37 low units). A 6-1 Council vote amended the ordinance and the fee formula to make payment more flexible (date not confirmed).
record.affordability_requirement: Affordability term at least 55 years for rental and 45 years for ownership; affordable rental units built by a separate affordable developer on a parcel within an ownership project may not request City financial assistance; at least 40% of such units must have two or more bedrooms; interior standards equal to LIHTC minimums.
record.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; fee per the current Council resolution at building permit. Council must review the Trust Fund and fee within 180 days after each fiscal year end (by late December).
record.layering_notes: A low 3-unit threshold but a fee-out for all ownership and all rental projects up to 100 units, so in practice most Huntington Beach projects pay the fee; the Trust Fund (next record) is the resulting local source. The ordinance's fee-reduction incentive is the only affordable housing fee relief found among the five cities. Housing Element status matters here: HCD's March 6, 2026 letter found the 2021-2029 element cannot be certified until the Program 2A and 2B rezonings (Affordable Housing Overlay) are complete, and the state litigation over the element continues, which exposes projects to builder's remedy and limits state funding points. Code read on the zoneomics mirror; Legistar attachments (HCD letter, 2025 APR) opened via the Legistar web API.
eligible_project_detail: market-rate rental and for-sale projects of 3 or more units (compliance)
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

record.program_name: Residential Density Bonus and Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreements (Garden Grove Municipal Code Chapter 9.60, Secs. 9.60.040 and 9.60.050; Housing Element Program 10)
record.administering_agency: City of Garden Grove Community and Economic Development Department, Planning Services Division
record.typical_award_size: Requirement and entitlement, not a subsidy. Chapter 9.60 implements the State Density Bonus Law, Housing Accountability Act, Housing Crisis Act and No Net Loss law: density bonus, incentives, concessions, waivers and parking ratios per Government Code 65915 and 65915.5 as amended, processed concurrently with the land use application; ministerial review for qualifying housing development projects; replacement of protected units; regulatory agreement required for every affordable unit (Sec. 9.60.050) including a rule that voucher holders pay the affordable rent, not FMR. The 2021-2029 Housing Element reports surveyed projects averaging 183% of base density through bonuses and commits the City to the updated ordinance by 2025 (Program 10) and to study an inclusionary ordinance (Program 11).
record.affordability_requirement: State thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% affordable) with 55-year rental covenants in the City regulatory agreement.
record.next_deadline: Applies at project application. Program 11 inclusionary study was due within the Housing Element cycle; no inclusionary ordinance or in-lieu fee exists as of this pass.
record.layering_notes: Garden Grove has no inclusionary ordinance, in-lieu fee, local housing trust fund or affordable housing fee waiver; density bonus plus Housing Element Program 4 (technical and financial assistance for 10 affordable units a year, expedited processing, land write-downs from General Fund, HOME, LMIHAF and PLHA) is the full local toolkit beyond the Housing Successor land and GGHA vouchers. Garden Grove is not a Prohousing designated city. Density bonus does not trigger prevailing wage. Chapter 9.60 read on the zoneomics mirror; 2021-2029 Housing Element PDF opened on ggcity.org.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).
